steps.context: Raw integer gene-level salmon counts, 12000 genes x 16 samples (data/inputs/counts/counts.csv), paired with a 16x4 metadata table carrying genotype (WT/KO), treatment (vehicle/drug), and condition (data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv). No batch variable in the profile.
steps.question: Do the 16 brain samples (4 genotype x treatment cells, n=4 each) cluster by genotype and treatment, and is any sample an outlier before fitting the interaction model?

PCA plot colored by genotype and by treatment, with % variance explained on axes

steps.name: DESeq2 interaction model: filter, normalize, fit, test, shrink
caveats: With only 4 replicates per cell, the interaction term (difference-of-differences) has low statistical power; a non-significant interaction does not establish that the drug effect is the same in both genotypes — state this explicitly in output
Unbalanced outlier flagging: cells with <7 replicates get NA p-values for Cook's-distance-flagged genes rather than replacement — report these separately from independent-filtering NAs
steps.context: Same 12000x16 raw count matrix and 16x4 metadata (genotype, treatment, condition columns). This is the central analysis answering the research question: does the drug act differently in KO vs WT.
steps.question: Fit design ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment on the WT/KO x vehicle/drug counts, and test whether the drug effect (drug vs vehicle) differs between KO and WT (interaction coefficient), alongside the drug effect within each genotype separately.

grounding.reason: 2x2 interaction design: fit genotype+treatment+genotype:treatment, test interaction coefficient with Wald test, report simple effects, shrink with ashr, BH-adjust per contrast (R-0013, R-0092, R-0040, R-0061)

constraints: Design formula: ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment
Explicit factor releveling: genotype relevel to 'WT' reference, treatment relevel to 'vehicle' reference, before DESeqDataSetFromMatrix

Use ashr for shrinkage on all three contrasts (interaction and each simple effect are not single named coefficients suitable for apeglm alone, except the interaction and treatment-main-effect coefficients which are single coefficients — apply ashr uniformly across all three for consistency and because the KO-simple-effect is a list-contrast)
Report the interaction coefficient name and both reference levels explicitly in the output table headers
acceptance_criteria: Genes pre-filtered to >=10 counts in >=4 samples (smallest cell size) before fitting
DESeq2 size factors (median-of-ratios) used for normalization; no external re-normalization of counts
Reference levels set explicitly: genotype=WT, treatment=vehicle
Interaction coefficient genotypeKO.treatmentdrug tested with the Wald test
Simple effect 'drug vs vehicle in WT' extracted from the treatment main-effect coefficient
Simple effect 'drug vs vehicle in KO' extracted as the sum of the main effect and interaction coefficient (via contrast or list-form results call)
ashr shrinkage applied to each of the three result tables (both simple effects and the interaction contrast), reporting both shrunken and unshrunken log2FC with lfcSE
BH-adjusted p-values (padj) reported per contrast at alpha=0.05 with independent filtering left on; p-value histogram inspected per contrast before trusting padj
Count outlier handling (Cook's distance NA-flagging, since n=4<7 per cell) left on and the count of NA-flagged genes reported per contrast
Number of genes tested after filtering and number of DE genes at padj<0.05 reported per contrast

caveats: Enrichment results are method- and metric-dependent; present significant sets as hypotheses for follow-up rather than proven findings

steps.context: Three DESeq2 Wald-statistic-ranked gene lists (drug-in-WT, drug-in-KO, interaction), each covering ~the filtered/tested subset of the 12000-gene brain count matrix. steps.question: For each of the three contrasts (drug effect in WT, drug effect in KO, genotype x drug interaction), which MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome pathways are enriched among the coordinated but possibly individually-subthreshold gene-level changes in this brain tissue dataset?

grounding.reason: Preranked GSEA per contrast on Wald statistic vs Hallmark then Reactome, per R-0098/R-0107/R-0104; env has msigdb-hallmark-human and reactome-pathways staged

constraints: Rank metric = DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column), stated choice per the disputed ranking-metric rule — not the unshrunken log2FC alone and not a signed p-value
Run once per contrast; do not pool contrasts into one ranked list
min.size=15, max.size=500 for both collections
acceptance_criteria: Genes ranked separately for each of the three contrasts by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column) — full tested gene list used, no pre-threshold cut
fgsea run against MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (50 sets) as the primary collection, with gene set size window 15-500 applied after intersecting with tested genes
fgsea run a second time against Reactome human pathways as a confirmatory collection
BH-adjusted enrichment p-values reported per contrast per collection, contrasts never pooled
Redundant/overlapping significant gene sets collapsed to representative sets (collapsePathways) with full table kept as supplement
Leading-edge genes reported for every significant gene set
Share of gene symbols that failed to map/resolve in each gene set collection reported

steps.name: Interaction analysis report
caveats: Underpowered interaction term at n=4/cell must be stated as a limitation, not omitted
steps.context: Synthesizes the DESeq2 interaction model results (T1S2) and the per-contrast fgsea enrichment results (T2S1) into the final answer to the research question.
steps.question: Summarize, in one decision-ready report, whether and how the drug's effect on brain gene expression differs between KO and WT animals.

grounding.reason: Report-step aggregation rules apply generically (R-0092 interaction reporting, R-0085 shrunken/unshrunken table, R-0087 diagnostics, R-0086 reproducibility record) but no single rule 'covers' report synthesis as a step type in this tool's matching logic

constraints: Report the interaction contrast, both simple effects, and both enrichment collections together — never present the interaction result alone as 'the answer'
acceptance_criteria: Report states the design formula, explicit reference levels (genotype=WT, treatment=vehicle), and all three contrast definitions side by side (drug-in-WT, drug-in-KO, interaction)
MA plot and dispersion plot included as fit diagnostics, plus p-value histograms per contrast
Gene tables carry unshrunken log2FC, ashr-shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, padj, and NA-flag reason (Cook's outlier vs independent filtering) for each of the three contrasts
Number of genes tested and number of DE genes (padj<0.05) reported per contrast

Enrichment section reports database name+version, rank metric, universe, and size window for both Hallmark and Reactome results, with leading-edge genes for significant sets and the caveat that results are method-dependent

Explicit power caveat: n=4/cell limits sensitivity of the interaction (difference-of-differences) test; a non-significant interaction is not interpreted as evidence of no genotype-dependent drug effect
Full reproducibility record included: sessionInfo, package versions (DESeq2, ashr, fgsea), gene set collection versions/paths, and any random seeds used

plan.title: 2x2 genotype x drug interaction DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is precisely an interaction question in a 2x2 factorial (genotype: WT/KO x treatment: vehicle/drug, n=4/cell, 16 samples, 12000 genes, raw salmon counts from brain tissue). The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 interaction procedure: (1) QC on sample structure via blind VST/PCA/distance heatmap to catch outliers or unexpected clustering before modeling, since one mislabeled or off-clustering sample in a 4-per-cell design would materially distort the interaction test; (2) minimal count pre-filter; (3) DESeq2 model with design ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, explicit reference levels (WT, vehicle) so the interaction coefficient genotypeKO.treatmentdrug directly answers the research question, tested by Wald test; (4) report three coefficients side by side per rule R-0092 — the drug effect in WT (reference), the drug effect in KO, and the interaction contrast — because the interaction term alone doesn't say whether the drug does anything in either genotype, and a simple effect alone doesn't say if it differs by genotype; (5) ashr shrinkage (contrasts, not single coefficients, so ashr not apeglm); (6) BH FDR with independent filtering per contrast; (7) fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (with Reactome as a confirmatory second collection) run separately per contrast, since pooling would cancel opposite-direction signals; (8) a report step that assembles diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histograms), the three-contrast interaction table, leading-edge genes, and full reproducibility metadata (sessionInfo, package versions, gene set collection versions, seeds). With only 4 replicates per cell the interaction coefficient (a difference-of-differences) has low power — flagged explicitly in the DE step and repeated in the report so a null interaction is not over-read as 'no genotype-dependent drug effect' when it may simply be underpowered.

steps.method: keep genes with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size (4)
design = ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, explicit reference levels WT and vehicle
DESeq2 Wald test on interaction coefficient genotypeKO.treatmentdrug, plus simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT, drug vs vehicle within KO)
Benjamini-Hochberg with independent filtering, alpha=0.05, within each contrast
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome, per contrast
interaction report with simple effects, interaction contrast, diagnostics, reproducibility record
